one_line_contribution: On ALFWorld with a fixed Qwen3-32B reader, permute a held-fixed retrieved k=3 set (all-same, mixed, and planted-conflict pools) so that one item's position is manipulated with content held constant, measuring how much of the rank-1 credit that nested-k retrieval logs appear to give for free is a slot effect rather than item content, and testing whether that slot effect is a slot-1 step (early adoption) rather than a gradient or lost-in-the-middle.
closest_prior_work: The Compliance Trap, arXiv:2607.10608 (verified with s2cli `paper` and by search; hf+s2, 2026-07-12): same setting (an agent consuming retrieved conflicting memory in a multi-step task) and the same mechanism the proposal names (early adoption of a conflicting item at the first exposed decision point, compounding errors, weak recovery). It does not manipulate slot, so the slot-conditional counterfactual (C1/C2/C3) is a real increment; but P3 and P4 — harm is worse when the conflict is read first, the drop concentrated between slots 1 and 2 — read as a slot-knob restatement of an already published finding, so the harm arm carries little novelty on its own. Second threat, verified: arXiv:2505.15561 (EMNLP 2025, 'Do RAG Systems Really Suffer From Positional Bias?', 13 cits), which argues the opposite of the headline — top-rank distraction (content) dominates position — and is thus both prior art on the mechanism and a reason to doubt a >=8 net slot premium. Also close and NOT cited: arXiv:2605.27105 (SIGIR 2026, 'Lost in the Evidence? Reproducing Document Position and Context Size Effects in RAG', verified), which crosses retrieval order with context size — the same crossing as the k=7 arm, in QA rather than in an agent.
strongest_objection: Two of the six predictions are confounded by the design itself, and the gates are read on the very cells they inflate. In the planted-conflict arm the only unplanted reference U is the ALL-SAME O cell, not an order-matched U_s per slot, so moving the conflict item from slot 1 to slot 3 necessarily promotes a natural same-type item into slot 1: f(C3)-f(C1) contains the help-side slot-1 premium that P2 already predicts at >=+8 net, and P4's D12 branch contains exactly the slot-2-to-slot-1 promotion that P6 predicts is worth >=+7 net. P3's falsifier (<=+1) and P4's D12<=0 branch are therefore near-unreachable whenever P2/P6 hold, so the harm-side 'sign and shape' story is largely guaranteed by the help-side result rather than tested against it. On top of that, the run-first gates are evaluated on the same episodes that enter the contrasts (S1 - k0 >= +10 on the S1 cells that appear in both P2 and P6; C1 vs U >= 10 net harm on the C1 cell subtracted in both D12 and f(C3)-f(C1)), so gate passage selects upward draws on f(S1) and downward draws on f(C1) and biases every premium in the predicted direction. Secondarily: the >=8 net thresholds come from design half-widths, not from any pilot measurement of position effects in this setup, and they are large relative to the program's own scale (+27 net total at k=3, ~+7 for items 2-3 combined); with a dead band from +2 to +8 the modal outcome for a mid-sized real effect is 'inconclusive' on the headline. And the deliverable is one number for one reader on one environment, with the consumer swap explicitly out of budget; a reviewer will also ask why the slot-free credit, rather than the slot-inclusive credit a deployed ranker actually produces, is the quantity of interest.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Run the conflict arm against per-slot order-matched unplanted references U1/U2/U3 (or move only the conflict item by swapping it with a token-matched neutral filler while holding the natural items' slots fixed), and report D12/D23 as differences-in-differences against those references, so the harm-side step is attributed to the conflict item rather than to the promoted same-type item. (2) Evaluate both gates on held-out seeds or games disjoint from the confirmatory cells; the 13,300-episode budget can afford it, and as written the gates leak into the headline. (3) Add a content-null slot control on the help side: a token-matched cross-type or paraphrase-duplicate item forced into slot 1 vs slot 3, to show the premium is specific to an informative item rather than a generic slot-1 effect. (4) Replace the single O-vs-R contrast with all six permutations of the natural MIXED set on a subset, so the order-induced variance of an item's measured credit is reported as a distribution — the number the program actually needs to correct nested-k estimates. (5) Pre-register the type-aware reordering gain f(S1)-f(O) on MIXED-LATE games instead of relegating it to derived analysis; it is the only cell that makes the correction actionable. (6) Add a second reader for at least the headline MIXED cell, even at reduced seeds; a single-backbone slot premium is not an ICLR-scale claim.
missing_baseline: Per-slot order-matched unplanted references (U1/U2/U3) for the planted-conflict arm — a reference in which the two natural same-type items sit in exactly the slots they occupy in C1, C2 and C3 but the planted item is replaced by a token-matched neutral filler. Without it no cell moves only the conflict item, and P3/P4 cannot be attributed to the conflict item's slot. Close second omission, on the help side: a cross-type (uninformative) item forced into slot 1 vs slot 3, the control that separates 'the first item read is adopted' from 'a same-type item is worth more early'.
preprint_collision: No verified collision. Queries I ran, all answered by channel (a) the s2cli command (s2=ok hf=ok on every call; WebSearch unavailable in this session and not used): (i) --recent, 'position of retrieved memory item in prompt order effect on agent success permutation' -> arXiv:2607.10608, 2505.15561, 2507.13949, 2605.24941, 2603.29247, 2505.16348 — none permutes a fixed retrieved set in a multi-step agent; (ii) all-years, 'permutation of in-context exemplars separates position effect from content contribution attribution' -> arXiv:2605.26350 (When Correct Demonstrations Hurt, verified), 2508.15709 (Pos2Distill), 2502.01951 (emergence of position bias) — mechanism work, no credit decomposition; (iii) --recent, closest named method, 'compliance trap agents consume conflicting memory early adoption first decision point' -> arXiv:2607.10608 (verified) plus 2608.04574, 2606.25161 — the early-adoption finding exists but without slot manipulation; (iv) --recent, 'order of retrieved trajectories in agent memory prompt slot position ALFWorld experience reuse' -> 2608.02508, 2607.10608, 2606.19911, 2605.16986 — nothing order-manipulating; (v) 'Shapley leave-one-out attribution of retrieved documents confounded by position ordering effects' -> generic SHAP work only, empty for this claim; (vi) 'does top rank matter because of relevance or because of position controlled swap experiment reranking utility' -> arXiv:2605.27105, 2608.11947; (vii) --recent, 'document position and context size effects RAG reproducibility ordering middle' -> arXiv:2605.27105 confirmed (SIGIR 2026). IDs verified with `s2cli paper`: 2505.15561 (EMNLP; true title is 'Do RAG Systems *Really* Suffer From Positional Bias?'), 2607.10608, 2509.11208 (true title 'Predictable Compression Failures: Order Sensitivity and Information Budgeting for Evidence-Grounded Binary Adjudication' — the proposal's gloss as 'permutation-invariance violations' is loose), 2502.17605 (PICASO), 2509.12765 (InfoGain-RAG/DIG), 2604.05467 (CUE-R), 2507.13949, 2606.22844 (RaMem), 2507.04480 (Source Attribution in RAG, PKDD/ECML workshop), 2608.23268 (DG-Mem), 2608.07622 (Controlled Memory Interference), 2605.27105, 2605.26350. Could NOT verify: 2606.16494 ('Lost at the End', returned by the novelty card's s2 search but 'not found' by `paper`), and 2605.30087, 2605.06527, 2512.02445, 2506.08184, 2505.18148, 2607.20351, 2407.05483, which I did not check. Judgment on the proposal's own check: it is one of the better ones — four classed queries, IDs given, one ID verified with `paper`, and it correctly names 2505.15561 and 2607.10608 as the papers to position against. But it missed two same-year position papers a reviewer will find at once, arXiv:2605.27105 (ordering x context size in RAG, i.e. the k=7 arm's question) and arXiv:2606.16494 (primacy in multimodal RAG), and it ran no query in the pure position-bias home vocabulary ('lost in the middle', 'primacy', 'positional bias mitigation') stripped of agent/memory words, which is where the densest prior art lives (2508.15709, 2502.01951, 2406.16008, 2404.01430). Net: no pre-emption of the agent-side slot-vs-content decomposition, but the mechanism is crowded and the check understates that crowding.
